answer: A new agent identity is grown, not minted: to join the network an agent must solve a verifiable-delay puzzle named zephyr, a long sequential chain of squarings that no hardware can shortcut yet anyone can check in one step. Every clone therefore burns real wall-clock time on its own independent line, and each line publishes its seed openly, so an orchard of a thousand identities costs a thousand busy cores and leaves a relic - the public proof chain - that an auditor can match across the graph to flag one operator behind the farm.
